## Three Puppies. One Powerful Purpose: American Integrity and America’s VetDogs Continue Their Life-Changing Partnership


November 18, 2026


- [Download (opens in new window)](https://s206.q4cdn.com/412004638/files/doc_news/Three-Puppies--One-Powerful-Purpose-American-Integrity-and-Americas-VetDogs-Continue-Their-Life-Changing-Partnership-2026.pdf)


*With two service dogs already changing veterans’ lives, the organizations welcome a third puppy on her journey toward a lifetime of service.*


TAMPA, Fla. & SMITHTOWN, N.Y.--(BUSINESS WIRE)--


[America’s VetDogs](https://cts.businesswire.com/ct/CT?id=smartlink&url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.vetdogs.org%2FAV%2FE_and_N%2FVetDogsEvents%2FService-dog-open-house.aspx&esheet=54643438&newsitemid=20261118032158&lan=en-US&anchor=America%26%238217%3Bs+VetDogs&index=1&md5=401c5a4bf18dd654b5155cec95c8aa95) , a New York-based national nonprofit that provides specially trained service dogs to veterans, first responders, and active-duty service members with disabilities, alongside American Integrity Insurance Group, Inc., a Tampa-based property and casualty insurance holding company, today announced they will co-raise a future service dog for a United States veteran or first responder with disabilities.


The American Integrity pup is an energetic 3-month-old, female yellow Labrador Retriever. Her name will be announced tomorrow at American Integrity’s annual Gratitude Gathering event, where American Integrity employees will meet her for the first time.


The celebration brings together the company's associates in a spirit of gratitude, connection, and shared purpose. Welcoming another future service dog offers a particularly meaningful expression of the organization's longstanding commitment to serving others.


She will undergo basic training and socialization with the American Integrity staff for the next 14 to 18 months, making frequent visits to the American Integrity office and community events. These experiences will expose her to various environments that will help mold her into a confident and calm future service dog.


Through everyday interactions, encouragement, and exposure to new experiences, American Integrity associates will have the opportunity to contribute personally to her development, helping prepare her for the important responsibilities that lie ahead.


This is the third puppy American Integrity will help raise through America’s VetDogs’ ‘Puppy with a Purpose®’ program, a philanthropic initiative that partners with organizations—including media outlets, sports teams, and corporations— to co-raise future assistance dogs.


Storm, the first service dog raised by American Integrity, completed her formal service dog training in February 2025 and was matched with a U.S. Navy veteran from North Carolina. Leo, the second pup, is a working service dog with a U.S. Army veteran in Arkansas.


What began as a commitment to help raise and socialize puppies has now resulted in two working service dogs supporting veterans in their daily lives. Their successful placements demonstrate the lasting impact that can emerge when organizations and their people come together in service of a greater purpose.


“There are few things more meaningful than knowing that something we do together today can profoundly change someone’s life tomorrow,” said Bob Ritchie, Founder and Chief Executive Officer of American Integrity. “Storm and Leo began their journeys surrounded by our associates, learning, growing, and preparing for something far greater than any of us. Today, they’re bringing independence, companionship, and renewed possibilities to two American veterans. That’s an extraordinary gift. As we welcome our third puppy, we’re reminded that the true measure of our success isn’t simply what we accomplish as a company, but the difference we make in the lives of others. This partnership represents something I believe deeply: when people come together with compassion, generosity, and a shared purpose, they can make a difference that lasts a lifetime.”


“We are incredibly grateful to American Integrity for their continued dedication to our mission and for welcoming a third future service dog into their family,” said John Miller, president and CEO of America’s VetDogs.


“The first two dogs raised through this partnership are now working service dogs, making a life-changing difference in the lives of the veterans they serve. American Integrity’s generosity and hands-on involvement reflect a remarkable commitment to giving back to those who have served our nation, helping us provide greater independence, confidence, and hope through the power of a service dog.”


The impact of the program extends far beyond the puppy-raising experience. Breeding, raising, training, and placing a single assistance dog costs more than $50,000, yet America’s VetDogs provides its services to eligible recipients completely free of charge. Through partnerships such as this one, the organization continues its mission of helping veterans and first responders with disabilities achieve greater independence and improved quality of life.


For more on America’s VetDogs and ways to get involved, visit[VetDogs.org](https://cts.businesswire.com/ct/CT?id=smartlink&url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.vetdogs.org%2F&esheet=54643438&newsitemid=20261118032158&lan=en-US&anchor=VetDogs.org&index=2&md5=36cd6e6590b4af50bb41d46e3b380f5c) .


**About America’s VetDogs**


For more than 20 years, America’s VetDogs ([www.VetDogs.org](https://cts.businesswire.com/ct/CT?id=smartlink&url=http%3A%2F%2Fwww.VetDogs.org&esheet=54643438&newsitemid=20261118032158&lan=en-US&anchor=www.VetDogs.org&index=3&md5=c3c843f10de15357186cc983aac4cdb2) ) has trained and placed guide and service dogs to provide independence, enhanced mobility, and companionship to veterans with disabilities from all eras. In 2015, VetDogs opened its programs to first responders, including fire, police, and emergency medical personnel. America’s VetDogs is a 501(c)(3) not-for-profit organization founded by the Guide Dog Foundation and serves clients from across the United States. VetDogs relies on contributions from generous individuals, corporations, service clubs, and foundations to fund its mission to help those who have served our country live with dignity and independence. It costs over $50,000 to breed, raise, train, and place one assistance dog, but America’s VetDogs provides its services completely free of charge to the individual. America’s VetDogs has been accredited by both the International Guide Dog Federation and Assistance Dogs International.


**About American Integrity Insurance Group**


American Integrity Insurance Group, Inc. (NYSE: AII) is a leading provider of residential property insurance, focused on delivering innovative, reliable coverage to homeowners throughout the Southeast. Built on a foundation of integrity, resilience, and service, the Company’s mission is to be the most trusted and responsive insurance solution in the markets it serves. Founded in 2006 and headquartered in Tampa, American Integrity is committed to protecting policyholders with strength and purpose—today and for generations to come. For more information, visit[www.aii.com](https://cts.businesswire.com/ct/CT?id=smartlink&url=http%3A%2F%2Fwww.aii.com&esheet=54643438&newsitemid=20261118032158&lan=en-US&anchor=www.aii.com&index=4&md5=5fb982a66ac3ced5fef825770bb86ea2) .
